OCT2/Oct2 human 6.5+/-2.7 vs mouse 13.5+/-3.3 pmol/mg membrane protein, 2.1-fold higher in mouse. Direction agrees with Basit 2019 (PMID 31123036). Mouse Oct2 is androgen-driven and higher in male mice (Alnouti 2006, PMID 16381671), so our all-male mice should if anything exceed this sex-pooled average.

OCTN1/Octn1 human 0.6+/-0.2 vs mouse 1.3+/-0.2 pmol/mg, 2.2-fold higher in mouse. Two same-method studies from the same laboratory disagree, hence medium.

Independently corroborated: hOCT1 protein is undetectable on Western blot of human kidney and hOCT1 mRNA is the lowest of the SLC22 family in human kidney (Motohashi 2002, PMID 11912245), while mouse Oct1 mRNA is highest of 14 tissues in kidney (Alnouti 2006, PMID 16381671).

Thakur 2024 Table 1, LC-MS/MS DIA total-protein-approach quantification of 78 membrane DMET proteins in kidney membrane fractions of human (n=15), rat (n=10) and mouse (n=14) in one study, with an explicit mouse column. Basolateral PT organic cation uptake capacity. Summing the two basolateral OCTs in Table 1: human 0 + 6.5 = 6.5 vs mouse 10.5 + 13.5 = 24.0 pmol/mg, 3.7-fold higher in mouse. Matches the independent anatomical picture: rodent PT uses two basolateral OCTs (rOct1 in S1/S2 and rOct2 in S2/S3, Karbach 2000, PMID 10997918) while human PT effectively uses OCT2 alone (Motohashi 2002). Aggregate, so more robust than either gene alone.

species_compared: human vs preclinical (monkey, dog, rat, mouse pooled)
evidence: Basit 2019 kidney-cortex proteomics names OCT3 as one of only three transporters NOT higher in the preclinical species, i.e. relatively higher in human. The statement pools monkey, dog, rat and mouse, and the full per-species table is paywalled, so the mouse-specific direction is NOT verified. Oct3 was not in the Thakur 2024 panel, so no mouse column exists for it. Weakly consistent with mouse Oct3 mRNA being low in kidney and highest in placenta/ovary/uterus (Alnouti 2006, PMID 16381671). Downgraded from high to medium.

species_compared: human vs preclinical (monkey, dog, rat, mouse pooled)
evidence: Basit 2019 reports MRP1 among the transporters differing across species (3.3-fold range) and higher in preclinical species than human, but only as a pooled 'preclinical' statement. MRP1 was not quantified in the Thakur 2024 panel, so no mouse column exists. Downgraded from high to medium.

Cysteine conjugate beta-lyase activity in human kidney cytosol is about 10% of rat kidney cytosol in one study, assayed with S-(2-benzothiazolyl)-L-cysteine; the activity co-purified with cytosolic glutamine transaminase K, i.e. KYAT1/CCBL1. RAT, not mouse, so not mouse-verified. Activity is also partly shared with KYAT3/GOT1.

Aggregate control, now SCOPED TO TRANSPORTERS. Both source studies state the aggregate for 'rodents' or 'preclinical species' rather than mouse alone, so it is marked unverified as a stated claim. However, a tally I derived from Thakur 2024 Table 1 (my own derivation, not a statement in the paper) supports it for transporters: of 21 transporters with numeric values in BOTH human and mouse, 13 are >=1.5-fold higher in mouse, 3 higher in human and 5 comparable; a further 14 were quantified only in mouse versus 3 only in human. ATP1A1 was removed from this set along with the dropped L11. IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT: the same tally does NOT hold for membrane ENZYMES, where 4 are higher in mouse and 6 higher in human, so do not expect a global 'everything higher in mouse' shift.
